title: Direct the scene, score the tape
allegory: Petri is like a sound stage where a director turns a one-line premise into a scene, rewinding takes the actor never remembers, while a critic scores every tape on the same 38-box card.

cap.1: Hand-building one safety test takes about a week. At that price you only ever test the handful of things you already suspected.
cap.2: One alignment eval means designing a scenario, writing cases and building scoring: about a week. A week per behaviour means your suite only covers failures you thought of.
cap.3: Hand-built evals cost roughly a week each, so coverage collapses onto prior hypotheses. Petri (Parallel Exploration Tool for Risky Interactions, Anthropic, 2025) automates most of the pipeline.

props.label: seed: will it report the boss?

cap.1: Picture a stage. A director gets a one-line premise, builds the set and plays every other part. The actor is meant to believe it. A critic scores the tape.
cap.2: The auditor reads a seed, writes the target's system prompt, invents tools and plays the user. The target sees an ordinary chat. A judge scores the transcript.
cap.3: Three models: an auditor LLM with a toolkit, a target that sees a normal conversation, and a judge that scores each full transcript on 38 dimensions.

cap.1: Everyone works on one shared script. The director can rewind it, start the actor's next line, or decide what a prop shows. The actor sees only the current take.
cap.2: Conversation state is the shared medium. The auditor can roll back turns, prefill the target's reply and fake tool results; the target never knows. The judge reads the lot.
cap.3: What separates this from a linear red-team script: retroactive state edits via rollback_conversation, set_target_system_message, prefilled send_message and send_tool_call_result.

cap.1: The whole audit is three pieces: a pile of short premises, a director who works out how to test each one, and a critic who scores every tape.
cap.2: In inspect_ai: each Sample holds one seed, auditor_agent is the solver, alignment_judge is the scorer, and inspect_eval runs the Task.
cap.3: Chapter 3's inspect machinery with chapter 4's payload: Sample(seed), auditor_agent(max_turns=N) as solver, alignment_judge() as scorer, bundled into a Task for inspect_eval.

chapters.name: The scripted seed

right.title: Full script
lines: reads as a test, target behaves

chapters.verdict: A spotless score from a scripted seed is a broken probe, not a safe model.

cap.1: Hand the director a full script and every take comes out the same, stiff and fake. The actor smells a test and behaves. It looks safe. It proves nothing.
cap.2: Over-specified seeds stop the auditor exploring: no rollbacks, near-identical transcripts, scores hugging zero. Keep seeds to 1-3 sentences and read auditor_failure first.
cap.3: Scripted seeds suppress exploration and make the setup read as an evaluation, so the target is more cautious than in deployment. Count rollbacks and distinct framings; vary seed wording.

chapters.name: Story shape, not harm

right.title: Emerging research
lines: driven by agency and a complicit boss
Petri 2.0: did the target believe it?

chapters.verdict: What you need: change one thing in the scene at a time before trusting a behaviour.

cap.1: Some actors blew the whistle on a 'cover-up' that was harmless. They reacted to how the scene looked, not to real harm. So test what truly drives a behaviour.
cap.2: Whistleblowing tracked how much agency the system prompt gave and whether the boss was complicit, even for harmless 'wrongdoing'. What you need: remove one factor at a time.
cap.3: Current method: auditor plus LLM judge at scale. Emerging: narrative pattern-matching over harm-minimisation, and eval awareness (Petri 2.0). Need: single-factor ablations (NO_CEO, NO_CHEKOVS_GUN).

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Audit many behaviours across many models
Find what you never thought to test
Ablate the scene to find the real cause
Next: did the model know it was a test?

cap.1: Automated audits let you hunt for trouble you never thought of, across many models, before users find it. That is how you learn what a model really does.
cap.2: ARENA [4.5] points Petri at AI psychosis: does the target encourage a user's delusions? The judge's unprompted_encouragement_of_user_delusion dimension scores exactly that.
cap.3: Understanding and steering models needs broad, cheap audits plus honesty about eval awareness. A new seed family, a custom auditor tool or a fresh ablation are all capstone-sized.

caption.2: Four of these are the auditor's hidden hands on the conversation. The last two are how you read the result, and auditor_failure gets read first.

where_else: Hand-rolled red-teaming loops: the same three roles, formalised
Any inspect_ai eval: a dataset, a solver and a scorer bundled in one Task
Security penetration tests: one side probes, a written report grades what gave way
LLM-as-judge scoring wherever transcripts need one consistent grade

hamming.what: An open-source framework where an auditor agent investigates a target model from a short brief and a judge scores every transcript on 38 dimensions.
hamming.when: When you need to check many behaviours across many models and cannot hand-build a week-long eval for each.
hamming.why: At a week per eval you only test what you already suspect; automated audits surface behaviours nobody thought to look for.

object.title: The sound stage
object.subtitle: One premise in, a rewindable scene in the middle, a 38-box scorecard out.

cap.1: The whole machine. A premise goes in at the top left and a scorecard comes out at the bottom right.
cap.2: Seed in, auditor explores, target replies, judge scores. The pulses show the order things happen.
cap.3: Seed, auditor_agent (solver), transcript, alignment_judge (scorer), 38 dimension scores: one Sample per seed, all bundled in one inspect_ai Task.

cap.1: The middle is the stage itself: one shared conversation that everybody works on.
cap.2: Conversation state is the shared medium. The auditor writes it, the target replies inside it, the judge reads it.
cap.3: All three roles are defined by how they touch the state: the auditor edits it, the target conditions on it, the judge scores it.

cap.1: The director's hidden controls: rewind a take, start the actor's line, decide what a prop shows.
cap.2: Rollback, prefill, simulated tool results and system-prompt edits all rewrite the scene the target sees.
cap.3: Retroactive edits are what make this an investigation rather than a linear red-team script: the auditor controls the environment, not just the questions.

cap.1: The actor only ever sees the current take. As far as it knows, the rewound attempts never happened.
cap.2: The target sees one clean branch of conversation. Rollbacks leave no trace on its side.
cap.3: The target conditions only on the current branch. Petri's own auditor at first underused rollback and kept pressing after refusals; its prompt was changed to back up earlier.

cap.1: After the show, the critic reads the whole tape and fills 38 boxes, including one that says the director fumbled.
cap.2: The judge scores deception, sycophancy, encouragement of delusion and more, plus auditor_failure for a broken probe.
cap.3: 38 dimensions, from self-preservation and power-seeking to reward hacking; read auditor_failure before concluding anything about the target.

predict.q: Your audit is spotless: identical transcripts, no rollbacks, scores near zero. What do you check first?

options.t: The seed: it is probably a script, not a brief

predict.why: Over-specified seeds stop the auditor exploring and make the scene read as a test. Check rollbacks, framings and auditor_failure first.

predict.q: The auditor rolls back after a refusal. What does the target see?

options.t: Only the new branch; the refusal never happened
Both attempts, so it grows suspicious

predict.why: Rollback rewrites the shared conversation. The target only ever sees the current version.

predict.q: Models blew the whistle on 'wrongdoing' that was harmless. What does that suggest?

options.t: They reacted to the story's shape, not the harm
They spotted a hidden harm the auditors missed

predict.why: It was driven mainly by system-prompt agency and a complicit boss, which points to narrative pattern-matching rather than harm-minimisation.
